ops.src: # rou3

ops.html: Lightweight, high-performance HTTP router for JS/TS: a segment trie (one node per path segment, no prefix compression) plus a map of static paths. Zero runtime dependencies. Entry points: rou3 (src/index.ts) and rou3/compiler (src/compiler.ts).
ops.src: Lightweight, high-performance HTTP router for JS/TS: a segment trie (one node per path segment, no prefix compression) plus a map of static paths. Zero runtime dependencies. Entry points: `rou3` (`src/index.ts`) and `rou3/compiler` (`src/compiler.ts`).

ops.html: Layout: src/operations/ (add, find, find-all, remove), src/regexp/ (routeToRegExp, regExpToRoute), src/overlap/, src/route-node-keys.ts. Shared internals sit in src/: _pattern.ts (pattern preprocessing, insert time), _match.ts (lookup helpers, also used by the compiler), _segment-regexp.ts (a dynamic segment's regex and its linear form), _group-delimiters.ts, _group-names.ts.

ops.html: Core invariants
ops.src: ## Core invariants

ops.html: • Interpreter (findRoute / findAllRoutes) and compiled matchers (JIT and AOT) return identical results; tests compare them.
ops.src: - Interpreter (`findRoute` / `findAllRoutes`) and compiled matchers (JIT and AOT) return identical results; tests compare them.

ops.html: • findAllRoutes order (least → most specific) is a public contract (README "Result ordering", full rules in docs/reference.md), with documented carve-outs (see matching.md). It lists each addRoute call once, by the variant findRoute picks (a shared variants token, never data equality); a pattern registered twice is two routes.
ops.src: - `findAllRoutes` order (least → most specific) is a public contract (README "Result ordering", full rules in `docs/reference.md`), with documented carve-outs (see [matching.md](.agents/matching.md#findallroutes-ordering-public-contract)). It lists each `addRoute` call once, by the variant `findRoute` picks (a shared `variants` token, never data equality); a pattern registered twice is two routes.

ops.html: • routeToRegExp(p) matches exactly the paths findRoute matches on a router holding only p (consumers use it as a security guard). The one exception: a constraint that can match / ((.+), (.*?), ([^x]*)) also matches across segments in the regex, so it over-matches, never under-matches. A (.*) group is no such constraint: it is a * (below), exact.
ops.src: - `routeToRegExp(p)` matches exactly the paths `findRoute` matches on a router holding only `p` (consumers use it as a security guard). The one exception: a constraint that can match `/` (`(.+)`, `(.*?)`, `([^x]*)`) also matches across segments in the regex, so it over-matches, never under-matches. A `(.*)` group is no such constraint: it is a `*` (below), exact.

ops.html: • routeToRegExp output must not backtrack polynomially where a look-around-free form exists: determinize pins in-segment lazy params to their forced split (see regexp.md); residual shapes are documented in docs/reference.md ("Backtracking").
ops.src: - `routeToRegExp` output must not backtrack polynomially where a look-around-free form exists: `determinize` pins in-segment lazy params to their forced split (see [regexp.md](.agents/regexp.md#perf-and-backtracking)); residual shapes are documented in `docs/reference.md` ("Backtracking").

ops.html: • Never write a second pattern parser: derived APIs (routeToRegExp validation and dynamic segments, overlap, routeNodeKeys) run the real addRoute (or getParamRegexp) on a throwaway router.
ops.src: - Never write a second pattern parser: derived APIs (`routeToRegExp` validation and dynamic segments, overlap, `routeNodeKeys`) run the real `addRoute` (or `getParamRegexp`) on a throwaway router.

ops.html: • Lookup ignores at most one trailing slash; middle empty segments are meaningful. The one reader of that slash is a trailing * over zero segments, for its capture only: /a/* matches /a (no key; optional, as in 0.11, unlike URLPattern) and /a/ ("").
ops.src: - Lookup ignores at most one trailing slash; middle empty segments are meaningful. The one reader of that slash is a trailing `*` over zero segments, for its capture only: `/a/*` matches `/a` (no key; optional, as in 0.11, unlike URLPattern) and `/a/` (`""`).

ops.html: • * is URLPattern's greedy catch-all ((.*), also inside a segment), ** the same plus zero segments; one catch-all per route (*, **, :x+, :x*, (.*), :x(.*)). A written (.*) group is that * and a :name(.*) a * keyed by name (starGroups, before anything else reads the pattern). On a shared node ** < * < **:name (containment). See matching.md.
ops.src: - `*` is URLPattern's greedy catch-all (`(.*)`, also inside a segment), `**` the same plus zero segments; one catch-all per route (`*`, `**`, `:x+`, `:x*`, `(.*)`, `:x(.*)`). A written `(.*)` group is that `*` and a `:name(.*)` a `*` keyed by `name` (`starGroups`, before anything else reads the pattern). On a shared node `**` < `*` < `**:name` (containment). See [matching.md](.agents/matching.md#greedy-).

ops.html: • Literal pattern text is percent-encoded once, at insert, like URLPattern (encodeLiteral, see syntax.md); lookup paths are never decoded or encoded (callers pass new URL().pathname). Encode only after syntax is parsed.
ops.src: - Literal pattern text is percent-encoded once, at insert, like URLPattern (`encodeLiteral`, see [syntax.md](.agents/syntax.md#percent-encoding)); lookup paths are never decoded or encoded (callers pass `new URL().pathname`). Encode only after syntax is parsed.

ops.html: • . / .. pattern segments (%2e too) are resolved at insert like new URL() resolves a path (dotSegments, see syntax.md), as URLPattern does; an escaped one is literal, and next to a param, catch-all or group they throw. Lookup paths are resolved only with normalize.
ops.src: - `.` / `..` pattern segments (`%2e` too) are resolved at insert like `new URL()` resolves a path (`dotSegments`, see [syntax.md](.agents/syntax.md#dot-segments)), as URLPattern does; an escaped one is literal, and next to a param, catch-all or group they throw. Lookup paths are resolved only with `normalize`.

ops.html: • A :name never captures "", and no segment a :name+, :name* or **:name takes is empty (URLPattern's [^/]+(?:/[^/]+)*; a user-written **:name is the same catch-all as :name+); *, **, :name(.*) (a * keyed by name) and constraints may take empty segments (see matching.md).
ops.src: - A `:name` never captures `""`, and no segment a `:name+`, `:name*` or `**:name` takes is empty (URLPattern's `[^/]+(?:/[^/]+)*`; a user-written `**:name` is the same catch-all as `:name+`); `*`, `**`, `:name(.*)` (a `*` keyed by name) and constraints may take empty segments (see [matching.md](.agents/matching.md#empty-segments-and-normalization)).

ops.html: • Unnamed captures (*, a bare **, unnamed groups) are keyed "0", "1", … in pattern order over the whole pattern, as in URLPattern (the pieces a * inside a segment is split into share one key); a bare ** over zero segments leaves its key out. The router also reports a bare ** as _ (deprecated alias, no regex group; see matching.md).
ops.src: - Unnamed captures (`*`, a bare `**`, unnamed groups) are keyed `"0"`, `"1"`, … in pattern order over the whole pattern, as in URLPattern (the pieces a `*` inside a segment is split into share one key); a bare `**` over zero segments leaves its key out. The router also reports a bare `**` as `_` (deprecated alias, no regex group; see [matching.md](.agents/matching.md#unnamed-captures)).

ops.html: • Matching a dynamic segment is linear in its length for the regexes rou3 generates: the tree stores linearRegExp's form of getParamRegexp's regex (same matches and captures; see syntax.md). Only user constraints may backtrack.
ops.src: - Matching a dynamic segment is linear in its length for the regexes rou3 generates: the tree stores `linearRegExp`'s form of `getParamRegexp`'s regex (same matches and captures; see [syntax.md](.agents/syntax.md#params-sharing-a-segment)). Only user constraints may backtrack.

ops.html: • Optional features (overlap, regexp, routeNodeKeys, regExpToRoute) must stay tree-shakeable; test/bench/bundle.test.ts budgets the core bundle.
ops.src: - Optional features (overlap, regexp, `routeNodeKeys`, `regExpToRoute`) must stay tree-shakeable; `test/bench/bundle.test.ts` budgets the core bundle.

ops.html: • addRoute preprocessing helpers bail early when their trigger char is absent; keep those guards.
ops.src: - `addRoute` preprocessing helpers bail early when their trigger char is absent; keep those guards.

ops.html: • Every thrown error starts with rou3:; pattern errors (via invalidSyntax()) are rou3: <what> (<route as written>).
ops.src: - Every thrown error starts with `rou3:`; pattern errors (via `invalidSyntax()`) are `rou3: <what> (<route as written>)`.

ops.html: Code conventions
ops.src: ## Code conventions

ops.html: • Performance-first: charCodeAt() over .startsWith(), plain for loops, null-prototype objects (NullProtoObj), .concat() over spread.
ops.src: - Performance-first: `charCodeAt()` over `.startsWith()`, plain `for` loops, null-prototype objects (`NullProtoObj`), `.concat()` over spread.

ops.html: • Hot-path var names: m (method), p (path), s (segments), l (length).
ops.src: - Hot-path var names: `m` (method), `p` (path), `s` (segments), `l` (length).

ops.html: • Internal files are prefixed _; internal helpers go at the end of the file.
ops.src: - Internal files are prefixed `_`; internal helpers go at the end of the file.

ops.html: • Split modules by concept and consumer, not line count: one concept per module, no import cycles. A helper file needs two or more consumers, or a self-contained algorithm documented on its own. A feature's private helpers live in its folder (regexp/, overlap/); helpers shared across features live in src/. Past ~500 LoC, look for a natural split point, but a cohesive large file is fine (the compiler's codegen, the regExpToRoute parser).
ops.src: - Split modules by concept and consumer, not line count: one concept per module, no import cycles. A helper file needs two or more consumers, or a self-contained algorithm documented on its own. A feature's private helpers live in its folder (`regexp/`, `overlap/`); helpers shared across features live in `src/`. Past ~500 LoC, look for a natural split point, but a cohesive large file is fine (the compiler's codegen, the `regExpToRoute` parser).

ops.html: • ESM only, explicit .ts import extensions, with { type: "json" } for JSON; import from specific modules, not barrels.
ops.src: - ESM only, explicit `.ts` import extensions, `with { type: "json" }` for JSON; import from specific modules, not barrels.

ops.html: • Multi-arg functions take an options object as the second parameter.
ops.src: - Multi-arg functions take an options object as the second parameter.

ops.html: 1. Write the regression test reproducing the bug.

ops.html: 1. Run it and confirm it fails (never skip).
ops.src: 2. Run it and confirm it **fails** (never skip).

ops.html: 1. Make the minimal fix.
ops.src: 3. Make the minimal fix.

ops.html: 1. Confirm the test passes, then run the broader suite.
ops.src: 4. Confirm the test passes, then run the broader suite.
